items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: Butchers, barbers. She had so many sons. She had some in every walk of life, you know what I mean?

ctx.x: But my grandmother wanted him to be like the rest of the family— carpenters, bricklayers, plasterers, and that kind of work, you know. Butchers, barbers. She had so many sons. She had some in every walk of life, you know what I mean? And she felt like, well, after my mother passed, that my brother should go along with one of my uncles. But just to think they had him dishwashing in a restaurant for three dollars a week, you know. And he—he didn't want his hands to become stiff or broken.
